nodes.label: File Locksmith OpenConsole locks
nodes.rationale: After a release Volt quit, Windows File Locksmith still shows OpenConsole.exe and cmd.exe children holding the project directory because Volt did not reap processes it started.

nodes.label: Owned Process
nodes.rationale: An Owned Process is a tree root (Windows Job Object with kill-on-job-close, or a Unix process group), so teardown kills the unit that holds locks, including OpenConsole and cmd grandchildren.

nodes.label: Process Registry
nodes.rationale: Sole ownership index keyed by OwnedProcessId, with workspace tags and an optional Share Key, so forgotten spawn sites cannot recreate orphans.

nodes.label: Process Launch
nodes.rationale: Every OS spawn must enter the Process Registry through Process Launch. Command::spawn outside Launch is a bug.

nodes.label: Share Key
nodes.rationale: Refcount for multi-workspace servers so closing the first workspace keeps a shared language server alive and closing the last workspace, or quitting, kills it.

nodes.label: Workspace
nodes.rationale: Workspace is the tagging unit. Close matches explicit Workspace tags only, so cwd or buffer-ancestry heuristics cannot kill unrelated processes.

nodes.label: Workspace Close
nodes.rationale: Tears down entries tagged for that Workspace. Share Key entries lose one tag and die only when no tags remain, so other workspaces keep their tools.

nodes.label: Application Quit
nodes.rationale: One global graceful-then-force sweep of the entire registry, in release builds as well as debug, so quit does not depend on iterating Workspace Close.

nodes.label: Hybrid Supervision
nodes.rationale: Platform kill-tree plus the existing volt --process-supervisor watchdog, per ADR 0007, so a UI-process crash still kills descendant trees on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Process-viewer nesting under Volt is best-effort.

nodes.label: Graceful-then-force shutdown
nodes.rationale: Protocol shutdown where it exists (LSP shutdown/exit, DAP disconnect, terminal close) runs with tree signaling, then force-kill on a hard deadline. A normal session cannot detach a child to outlive Volt.

nodes.label: No idle killer
nodes.rationale: While Volt stays open, quiet processes stay alive so a waiting build or paused terminal is left running. Idle auto-cleanup is out of scope.

nodes.label: Terminals, jobs, LSP, DAP, ACP, and helpers
nodes.rationale: Interactive terminals, background and compile jobs, language servers, debug adapters, ACP agent processes, and tool-install helpers are all owned children and must be started through Process Launch.

nodes.label: Process Registry test seam
nodes.rationale: Tests assert external liveness only at the Process Registry surface: launch, tag and Share Key refcount, Workspace Close, Application Quit, and crash-orphan. They skip internal maps, Job Object handles, and supervisor argv.

nodes.label: ADR 0007
nodes.rationale: Decision record docs/adr/0007-owned-process-hybrid-supervision.md: hybrid supervision is platform kill-tree plus volt --process-supervisor, with a single Process Launch into the Process Registry.
